{{Short description|Probability equation in mathematics}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Paley–Zygmund inequality''' bounds the
probability that a positive random variable is small, in terms of
its first two [[moment (mathematics)|moments]]. The inequality was
proved by [[Raymond Paley]] and [[Antoni Zygmund]].

'''Theorem''': If ''Z''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;0 is a [[random variable]] with
finite variance, and if <math>0 \le \theta \le 1</math>, then

:<math>
\operatorname{P}( Z > \theta\operatorname{E}[Z] )
\ge (1-\theta)^2 \frac{\operatorname{E}[Z]^2}{\operatorname{E}[Z^2]}.
</math>

'''Proof''': First, 
:<math>
\operatorname{E}[Z] = \operatorname{E}[ Z \, \mathbf{1}_{\{ Z \le \theta \operatorname{E}[Z] \}}]  + \operatorname{E}[ Z \, \mathbf{1}_{\{ Z > \theta \operatorname{E}[Z] \}} ].
</math>
The first addend is at most <math>\theta \operatorname{E}[Z]</math>, while the second is at most <math> \operatorname{E}[Z^2]^{1/2} \operatorname{P}( Z > \theta\operatorname{E}[Z])^{1/2} </math> by the [[Cauchy–Schwarz inequality]]. The desired inequality then follows. ∎

== Related inequalities ==

The Paley–Zygmund inequality can be written as

:<math>
\operatorname{P}( Z > \theta \operatorname{E}[Z] )
\ge \frac{(1-\theta)^2 \, \operatorname{E}[Z]^2}{\operatorname{Var} Z + \operatorname{E}[Z]^2}.
</math>

This can be improved since, by the [[Cauchy–Schwarz inequality]],

:<math>
\operatorname{E}[Z - \theta \operatorname{E}[Z]]
\le \operatorname{E}[ (Z - \theta \operatorname{E}[Z]) \mathbf{1}_{\{ Z > \theta \operatorname{E}[Z] \}} ]
\le \operatorname{E}[ (Z - \theta \operatorname{E}[Z])^2 ]^{1/2} \operatorname{P}( Z > \theta \operatorname{E}[Z] )^{1/2}
</math>

which, after rearranging, implies that

:<math>
\operatorname{P}(Z > \theta \operatorname{E}[Z])
\ge \frac{(1-\theta)^2 \operatorname{E}[Z]^2}{\operatorname{E}[( Z - \theta \operatorname{E}[Z] )^2]}
= \frac{(1-\theta)^2 \operatorname{E}[Z]^2}{\operatorname{Var} Z + (1-\theta)^2 \operatorname{E}[Z]^2}.
</math>



This inequality is sharp; equality is achieved if Z almost surely equals a positive constant.

In turn, this implies another convenient form (known as [[Cantelli's inequality]]) which is
:<math>
\operatorname{P}(Z >  \mu - \theta \sigma)
\ge \frac{\theta^2}{1+\theta^2},
</math>
where <math>\mu=\operatorname{E}[Z]</math> and <math>\sigma^2 = \operatorname{Var}[Z]</math>.
This follows from the substitution <math>\theta = 1-\theta'\sigma/\mu</math> valid when <math>0\le \mu - \theta \sigma\le\mu</math>.

A strengthened form of the Paley-Zygmund inequality states that if Z is a non-negative random variable then
:<math>
\operatorname{P}( Z > \theta \operatorname{E}[Z \mid Z > 0] )
\ge \frac{(1-\theta)^2 \, \operatorname{E}[Z]^2}{\operatorname{E}[Z^2]}
</math>
for every <math> 0 \leq \theta \leq 1 </math>.
This inequality follows by applying the usual Paley-Zygmund inequality to the conditional distribution of Z given that it is positive and noting that the various factors of <math>\operatorname{P}(Z>0)</math> cancel.

Both this inequality and the usual Paley-Zygmund inequality also admit <math> L^p </math> versions:<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Petrov |first1=Valentin V. |title=On lower bounds for tail probabilities |journal=Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference |date=1 August 2007 |volume=137 |issue=8 |pages=2703–2705 |doi=10.1016/j.jspi.2006.02.015 }}</ref> If Z is a non-negative random variable and <math> p > 1 </math> then
:<math>
\operatorname{P}( Z > \theta \operatorname{E}[Z \mid Z > 0] )
\ge \frac{(1-\theta)^{p/(p-1)} \, \operatorname{E}[Z]^{p/(p-1)}}{\operatorname{E}[Z^p]^{1/(p-1)}}.
</math>
for every <math> 0 \leq \theta \leq 1 </math>. This follows by the same proof as above but using [[Hölder's inequality]] in place of the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.
